title: Constant module inverse image in open-slice coordinates
statement: Let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and let $A$ be any commutative ring. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $C_W=\mathsf{sfCbcModelModules}(W,A)$ for the fixed constant-module equivalence to the published small model, and let $P_j=\mathsf{sfCbcMorphism}(j).\mathsf{modulePull}(A)$ be its fixed constant-module inverse image [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit]. Let $W_j$ be the pro-etale object given by $j$, let $B_T=\underline A_T$, and write $S_j=\mathsf{sfCbcConstantModuleToSlice}(T,W_j,A)$ for the fixed constant-coefficient transport from modules on $V$ to modules over $B_T|_{W_j}$ on the slice [lem-sf-cbc-extension-zero-completion]. For $R_j$ the literal restriction of $B_T$-modules to that slice [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], there is a natural isomorphism $C_T\mathbin{\ggg}P_j\mathbin{\ggg}C_V^{-1}\mathbin{\ggg}S_j\cong R_j$. All equivalences and scalar maps are the existing constant-section-normalized ones. No finiteness of $A$, quasi-compactness of $j$, nonemptiness of the schemes, extension functor, or derived category is assumed.

proof.text: Define the canonical constant-ring direct-image map on the AsSmall model by the constant-presheaf sheafification unit. The scalar normalization lemma identifies its set-sheaf transpose with the prescribed algebraic inverse-image scalar map. Apply the existing supplied tensor/module adjunction to this fixed algebraic lift, and identify its scalar-extension functor with ConstantCompletion.change.

Identify the fixed sfCbcModelModules transport with continuous module pushforward along AsSmall.down and the prescribed constant-ring comparison. The square of canonical constant-ring maps commutes: precompose with the constant sheafification unit and use sfCbcModelRingMap_existsUnique on both schemes. Continuous module-pushforward composition then gives the square of right adjoints. Conjugating the model adjunction by the two fixed equivalences and applying leftAdjointUniq identifies the transported modulePull with the ordinary constant-module left adjoint.

Reuse the proved openMap/baseChange site adjunction, its invertible constant-ring transpose, and the generic continuous module adjunction from VaryingRingOperations. Construct explicitly the natural isomorphism between Over.forget and cbcSliceFunctor followed by openMap; its components are identity maps on the underlying schemes. Naturality of the constant sheafification unit and the defining unit equation for sfCbcConstantSliceMap identify the resulting coefficient composite with the fixed slice coefficient map. Continuous module-pushforward composition and congruence therefore identify the ordinary constant-module left adjoint followed by sfCbcConstantModuleToSlice with literal localizedModuleRestriction. Whisker the model comparison by the fixed slice transport and compose the two isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem sfCbcOpenRestrictionModelComparison {V T : Scheme.{u}} (j : V ⟶ T)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    Nonempty (sfCbcModelModules T A ⋙
        (sfCbcMorphism j).modulePull (ULift.{u + 1} A) ⋙
          (sfCbcModelModules V A).asEquivalence.inverse ⋙
            sfCbcConstantModuleToSlice T (cbcOpenObject j inferInstance) A ≅
      SheafOfModules.localizedModuleRestriction (adicConstantRing T A)
        (cbcOpenObject j inferInstance))

tool_uses.why: Generic ringed-site localization to express constant module inverse image in slice coordinates; no geometric route of the parent unit is replaced.
Generic comparison for actual ringed inverse image supplies the slice equivalence before identifying the fixed constant coefficient transports.
Only its ordinary algebraic inverse-image lift and canonical constant-ring structural map are used to compare the fixed module pullback; no completion conclusion is used.
Generic module pullback and its specified induced scalar action identify the linearity of the underlying inverse-image comparison.
